title: Knife Skills: Cutting & Spreading
strapline: A table knife, a banana and a piece of toast — real skills for a real snack, trusted to do it themselves.
intent: Cutting and spreading with a table knife builds precise hand strength, wrist control and the pincer grip that later underpins writing.
Being trusted with a real, if child-safe, knife and a genuine job gives children a powerful sense of competence and responsibility.
Preparing their own snack — slicing fruit, spreading butter, halving a sandwich — folds independence and self-care into the day.
Judging where to cut and how thickly to spread invites early ideas of half, whole, thick, thin, more and less.
Handling and tasting the food they prepare tempts children to eat and talk about a wider range of foods.
Working calmly alongside others at a preparation table is quiet, focused, sociable work.
implementation: Offer child-safe knives and soft, sliceable foods — banana, cucumber, soft cheese, bread — and teach a safe grip and a still, flat board.
Model slowly and let children do it for real, resisting the urge to take over when it is slow or uneven.
Give the cutting a purpose — making the snack, filling the sandwiches, chopping for the soup — so the skill serves something.
Talk the maths as it happens: 'you cut the banana in half — now can you make four pieces?'
Set up a calm, well-organised preparation station with everything to hand so children can work independently.
Let children eat what they prepare and encourage them to try the foods they've handled.
key_questions: You cut the banana in half — now can you make four pieces?
How thickly shall we spread the butter?
Is this piece bigger or smaller than that one?
How will you hold the knife to keep your fingers safe?
How many pieces do we need so everyone gets one?

playing_exploring: Children handle real tools and foods and test how to cut, halve and spread for themselves.

creating_thinking: Children work out how to make halves and quarters, and adjust their grip and pressure to get a cleaner cut or a smoother spread.
